evidence: Hor. Ep. 1.16.49: sum bonus et frūgī

terms.grammar: indeclinable: frūgī, the dative of frux, with bonae
evidence: Plaut. Trin. 2.2.40: nec probus est nec frūgī bonae (Lewis & Short)
Plaut. Ps. 1.5.51: tamen erō frūgī bonae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The full old phrase behind frūgī: literally “of good use”.

phrases.english: Good boy: you’ve put all your things away.

sources: Lewis & Short: frugi · Lewis & Short: moratus
